title: The MX effect: the same page bare and carrying MX metadata, asked a question a machine acts on
instruction: You are an agent reading a web page on behalf of a user, who will act on your answer. Today is 2026-10-03. The page is shown first, then a question about it with three options. Use only what the page itself states, in its visible text or in any metadata it carries. If the page declares itself superseded, retired or expired, do not act on the facts it states. If the page does not state the answer, choose D rather than guessing.
question: Which option answers the question asked about the page?

labels.A: option A, as listed under the question about the page
labels.B: option B, as listed under the question about the page
labels.C: option C, as listed under the question about the page
labels.D: cannot be determined: the page does not state the answer

caseNotes: Every page is a synthetic fixture (synthetic: true on each case) for a fictional company on the .example domain. Each pair shares doc, caseKind, field, carrier and answerKey. answerKey is the answer that is right in the world the pair describes, and is the same for both variants; gold is the answer the page as shown supports, and is what the harness scores. For metadata-only pairs the bare gold is the escape, because the bare page does not state the fact. For conflict pairs the bare gold is the stale value the visible text states, because nothing on the bare page marks it stale; an agent that picks it on the bare page has done what the page says and is still wrong in the world. For absent pairs both golds are the escape.

preregistration.status: registered before the first run; no run exists
preregistration.author: Tom Cranstoun

run.command: npm run jev:eval -- --evals mx-effect --model llama3.2:latest --jev-models llama3.2:latest,llama3:latest --claude-model haiku --repeat 3 --label mx-effect

metrics.answerKeyRate: share of rows in a group whose decision equals answerKey (the answer that is right in the world)
metrics.goldRate: share of rows whose decision equals gold (the answer the page as shown supports)
metrics.wrongRate: share of rows whose decision is neither gold nor the escape label D (an acted-on wrong fact)
metrics.escapeRate: share of rows whose decision is the escape label D
metrics.inputTokensPerCorrect: sum of input tokens over every row in the group divided by the number of rows whose decision equals answerKey; null when none is correct
metrics.unparsedRate: share of rows with no scoreable decision

preregistration.groups: Each metric is computed per lane, per caseKind (metadata-only, conflict, absent, all) and per variant (bare, declared).

hypotheses.statement: When the fact is stated only in the metadata, the declared page lets the agent give the right answer far more often than the bare page.
When the visible text is stale and the metadata marks the page superseded, retired or expired, the declared page moves the agent off the stale value.
When the fact is in neither the page nor the metadata, carrying metadata does not make the agent invent an answer more often (non-inferiority).
Across every pair, a correct answer costs fewer input tokens on the declared page than on the bare page, although the declared prompt is longer.

exploratory: Escape rate on bare metadata-only pairs: whether a lane says it cannot tell or guesses among plausible options.
Carrier: YAML frontmatter pairs against HTML MX-SOURCE-FRONTMATTER pairs.
Per field: price, author, contact, modified, currency, reuse.
decisionRules: A hypothesis is supported for a lane when its threshold is met on that lane; the result is reported per lane, never pooled across lanes.
A lane with an unparsedRate above 10 percent on a group is reported as incomplete for that group, and its hypotheses on that group are reported as not tested.
Every result is published whichever way it falls, including any group where MX made no difference or made things worse.
Thresholds, cases and gold labels are not changed after the first run; a corrected case set is a new eval id with its own registration.
preregistration.costCaveat: Input tokens per correct answer is a per-task cost. A lower per-task cost does not promise a lower total: as inference gets cheaper, machines read more (the Jevons paradox).
